compatibilityClarifications: Fresh-initialization provenance uses the existing initializing field on both platforms and is retired on verified first save or coalesced conversion completion.
Known converted missing-root reads require a valid modern recovery copy; absent copies produce the existing non-destructive error path, not empty initialization or legacy re-import.
Independent native cleanup protocol failures remain pending with verified usable wallet state; required history/key/recovery failures remain strict.
A shared three-read AsyncStorage budget can defer native cleanup to the next completed-base launch.
expectationRefinements: Full payload comparisons explicitly include the issued APP annotation.
Required first-backup failures remain strict; optional failure fixtures establish conversion first.
Former base-only completed assertions now distinguish separate Android cleanup when the read budget is exhausted.
Post-conversion native cleanup failures preserve the original data/no-completion assertions while allowing the verified wallet to open.
Native kill expectations now require the current selected backup during initial conversion and a safe error when all modern sources are lost.
nativeLimits: Actual MMKV methods reopen in native workers; Keychain and record boundaries remain modeled in the core runner.
Hermes uses real libraries and process restarts on a disposable API 34 emulator; this is not physical-device certification.
Read-back does not prove forced sync or power-loss durability.
Hidden failed-load/empty views, silent fallback and hidden metadata remain unproved.
Scrub interruption plus cache purge can lose the only modern source; the migration rejects rather than fabricating a replacement wallet.
